prefilled.name: AGAPITO MORANO LAGUNSAD
prefilled.clientStatusOnExit: 14 - No Eligible (0-18 y/o) for CVS Monitoring (Certified by RPMO)

caseDevelopment.html:
The Ancog family was checked using the Family Risk and Vulnerability Assessment (FRVA). The results showed they have low risk in finances and the environment, and no risks in health, safety, or protecting children.
Their latest Social Welfare and Development Indicator (SWDI) assessment was done on October 10, 2025. It showed their family’s income is at Level 2, meaning they just meet basic needs (subsistence level). Their average monthly income per person is Php1,713.33. The poverty line in Bohol is Php2,170.74 per person each month, and the average food cost in the province is Php1,515.83.
The family has four more years to be in the program basing on the 7-year limit R.A 11310 and since they are still legible for the program due to their three children Nico, Tito Jr. and Blessy.
Edna is a 43-year-old grantee who has been a partner-beneficiary of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) for two years. Their main concern is the family’s insufficient income coming from unstable type of work and only her husband making for a living, which makes it difficult for them to cover essential needs such as healthcare and education for their children Nico, Tito Jr. and Blessy. This situation has continued over time, mainly due to their limited sources of income where Edna only assists her husband depending on the season of selling harvested root crops and vegetables. While her husband, Tito, works as a farmer. Based on the latest Social Welfare and Development Indicator (SWDI), their family is at level 2 (Subsistence Level). Their combined earnings are just enough to meet basic needs, with an average monthly income per person of Php1,713.33, which is below the poverty line which resulted insufficient to comfortably afford health and educational expenses. With the rising health and education costs have put a real strain on their finances. Plus, living on a remote Barangay and relying only on farming, which is easily get affected by weather and environmental condition, it poses burden in terms of family’s finances. The Ancog family have been struggling for a while but this burden was unloaded through the aid of the program; but things are getting more pressing now that their children Nico, Tito Jr. and Blessy must continue in their studies which needs increasing financial demands of supporting such as their school expenses such as food, school supplies, allowances, and other educational needs.
The family’s situation is not entirely permanent. The family may have big problems which mainly comes from social and economic issues that can be solve with the right help, support, and community programs. Ancog family is resilient, and they're involved in their community, which shows they want to change and improve for their family. Edna, in particular, has demonstrated her hardworking nature and willingness to seek solutions, which suggests that with appropriate support given, positive change is achievable.
Their environment also offers some available resources that can promote improvement. Local government programs which facilitate waste management, health services, and possible livelihood initiatives. The community has also basic facilities such as a health station, barangay hall, and water refilling stations, which can support health and sanitation needs. However, restraining forces such as limited income, geographic location, and dependence on vulnerable livelihood sources poses significant barriers to the family’s progress. These factors can make it hard to find stable jobs and get the services they need. Though the family’s problem is not immediately life-threatening but the on-going financial difficulties affects their ability to access necessary health and educational services, which are critical for their long-term well-being. Addressing these issues immediately is important to prevent further threatening of their level of well-being.
Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs explains that people are motivated by different needs arranged in levels. A person usually focuses first on satisfying the most basic needs before moving toward higher goals like achievement and self-fulfillment. The Ancog family is struggling because they don't have much money, so it's hard for them to regularly meet these basic needs. This affects how happy and healthy they are, and how they develop as people. But despite being financially incapable, the Ancog family was able to send their three children to school through the help of the program.
In Physiological Needs (survival needs), the household experiencing financial struggles and meeting their daily needs becomes their priority. For security and safety needs, parents want their children to have a comfortable life if they finish their studies and will have a better-paying job in the future. looks at the Ancog family as a group where everyone affects everyone else. Because they're having financial difficulties, it changes how they interact, their relationships, and how they handle tough times together. If we understand how they're all connected, we can create support programs that help the whole family.
For the esteem needs, the Ancog family’s strategies in overcoming struggles are done through collaborative and proactive approach. They involved everyone in seeking solutions of their problem which make them a functional family and could be a good asset to the family in attaining improved level of well-being. The LGU may provide assistance through referral services such as financial aid for school assistance every year as a support resource to address the children of the household to continue their studies, referral to healthcare for the family to stay healthy, and referral to economic opportunities so that families will have an equal opportunity to have a better life. which help strengthens their readiness for change.
